clue.text: Cold and dull: monarch cancelled performance

parts.note: matt means dull, without shine
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
an event cancelled is off
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A dreary complaint that a royal performance has been called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold and dull' looks like a two-part definition, but only 'Cold' defines; 'dull' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter-of-fact manner is unemotional and detached, which is a cold way of behaving.

clue.text: English writer cross with German's superior

indicators.note: in a down answer, superior means placed above the following piece

parts.note: mit is the German word for with
a ford is a place to cross a river

explanation.surface: An English author angered by a German boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry but is a place where a river is crossed; 'superior' means placed above, which works because this is a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Nancy Mitford was an English novelist, author of The Pursuit of Love.

clue.text: Rather like sun lamp, arguably, in skin treatment centre

parts.note: a sun lamp could be called a tanner since it tans the skin
the suffix -y means rather like, as in summery

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a sunbed salon is a bit like a sun lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is a works where animal hides are treated to make leather.

clue.text: With this application one can make way in class

definitions.text: With this application one can make way in class

parts.note: an entry is a way in
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: Filling in a form is how you get admitted to a class.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry form is the application document submitted to join a competition or course.

clue.text: Prisoner's here?

parts.note: asks where a captive is kept, pointing to a German wartime camp for captured officers

explanation.definitionFit: An Oflag was a German prisoner-of-war camp for officers in the World Wars.

clue.text: Air bed for lovers, typically

parts.note: to fan is to air or blow air at
a base is a bed, as in a bed of concrete

explanation.surface: An inflatable mattress designed for couples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air bed' looks like a mattress; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan base is the body of devoted followers, people who love a band or team.

clue.text: Unusual size car nuts

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of the following words appear in an odd new order

explanation.surface: An oddly sized car attracts enthusiasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazies are nuts in the noun sense: lunatics or wild people.

clue.text: In very upbeat mood, try some golf and cycle

parts.note: merry means cheerful and upbeat
a go is a try
a round is a spell of golf

explanation.surface: Feeling cheerful, someone has a go at golf and a bike ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A merry-go-round is an endless round of activity, a repetitive cycle.

clue.text: Cold in the shade after old flame's gone out

indicators.note: after puts the old flame first, before the shade

parts.note: an ex is a former lover, an old flame

indicators.note: in means the cold letter goes inside the shade

parts.note: a tint is a shade of colour
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Someone cools off in the shade once a former partner leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone out' as in a fire or a species no longer living; 'old flame' plays on that.
explanation.definitionFit: Extinct means no longer burning, like a volcano or fire that has gone out.

clue.text: Be impatient to prepare range of powers

parts.note: to long for something is to be impatient for it
to arm is to prepare for conflict

explanation.surface: Someone eager to get ready for a shooting range.
explanation.definitionFit: The long arm of the law is its far-reaching authority, a range of powers.

clue.text: Renaissance, mark, not right for selfish folk

indicators.note: not right says take away R, standing for right, and for says put the next piece in its place

parts.note: a renaissance is a regeneration or rebirth
M is short for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A historian notes the Renaissance was not right for egotists.
explanation.definitionFit: The me generation is a label for a self-absorbed age group, people focused on themselves.

clue.text: Eggs, well covered, line set of nests

indicators.note: covered means the eggs go round the next piece

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
OK means well or fine
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Instructions to line a nest with well-covered eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookery is a colony of rooks' nests high in trees.

clue.text: Fitting light green opening in middle of lounge?

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of green is used

parts.note: someone in the middle of lounging is lazing

explanation.surface: Choosing a pale green light fitting for the centre of a sitting room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lounge' is a sitting room in the surface but a verb in the wordplay; the question mark flags the loose sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Glazing is the work of fitting glass, which lets light into windows.

clue.text: Lynda doing backward skipping every second gets dizzy

indicators.note: backward says the letters picked are read from the end
skipping every second letter means taking alternate letters of the words

explanation.surface: Lynda skips backwards and ends up feeling dizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of LYNDA DOING give YDDIG, which 'backward' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Giddy is a direct synonym of dizzy, feeling the world spin.

clue.text: Marine's leg getting strong in slow time

indicators.note: in tells us the strong letter goes inside the marine phrase

parts.note: marine means of the sea
F is forte, strong in music
the on side, or leg side, in cricket

explanation.surface: A marine's injured leg gets stronger during a quiet spell.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side. 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The off season is the quiet time of year when business is slow.

clue.text: Desire which imparts goodness

parts.note: to fancy something is to desire it
that can be used for which, as in the book that I read

explanation.surface: A craving that is meant to be wholesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goodness' looks like virtue but is the exclamation 'Goodness!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, said when hearing something unexpected.

clue.text: Part of Ireland rebelled, driving away English general

indicators.note: driving away means one letter is removed from the word

parts.note: to rise or rise up is to rebel
common means general, shared by all

explanation.surface: An Irish rising drives out an English commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' is a soldier in the surface but an adjective in the wordplay. ROSCOMMON is a county in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Roscommon is a county in the Irish province of Connacht.

clue.text: Odds and ends of Victoriana you found in old jug

parts.note: SP is starting price, the betting odds

indicators.note: ends of means taking the last letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Bits of Victorian bric-a-brac you discovered inside an antique jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' is slang for prison, not a pitcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Spandau was a Berlin prison, long home to Nazi war criminals; jug is slang for jail.

clue.text: Pit coal put out of sight

indicators.note: put out means the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Coal from the pit has been dumped where nobody can see it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of sight' reads as one phrase; 'out' belongs with 'put' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical means relating to vision, so it is a fair match for of sight.

clue.text: Might salesman, holding now, finally ring back?

indicators.note: back means the whole result is read from right to left
holding means the salesman goes around the following letters

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word now

parts.note: O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: Should a salesman, now on hold, ring back?
explanation.definitionFit: Power and might are synonyms for strength or force.

clue.text: Lifted up version of Bible that is wide in scope

indicators.note: lifted, in a down answer, means read upwards

parts.note: RV is the Revised Version of the Bible
ie is id est, Latin for that is
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: An elevated Bible translation that is broad in its scope.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide is a ball in cricket bowled out of the batter's reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Purview is the range of authority or concern, the scope of something.

clue.text: Important point several score

parts.note: W is west, a compass point
a score is twenty, so eighty is four score

explanation.surface: A key point scores a high number of marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Weighty means important or serious, carrying great consequence.

clue.text: Duet can come unstuck as part not taken?

indicators.note: come unstuck suggests the letters fall apart and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A duet that falls apart means a role goes unperformed.
explanation.definitionFit: A part not taken on stage is unacted, never performed by any actor.

clue.text: Ultimately cagey entering as bell may sound on way out

indicators.note: entering means the last letter goes inside the bell's sound

parts.note: a bell's sound is a ding

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of cagey

explanation.surface: A reluctant passer-by hears a bell ring on leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on way out' sounds like leaving a building; it means close to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dying is close to death, on their way out of life.

clue.text: You get snogged loudly — and v. red rose!

indicators.note: loudly says the phrase is to be said out loud to hear the answer

parts.note: snogged is British slang for kissed, so you're kissed

explanation.surface: A rose fan exclaims about a kiss and a deep red bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yorkists' emblem was the white rose; their rivals the Lancastrians wore the red rose in the Wars of the Roses. 'v.' is versus.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkists were the side in the Wars of the Roses fighting against the red rose of Lancaster.

clue.text: Traveller swindled pair from Rome clothes company

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them, so did

indicators.note: clothes means the Roman pair wraps around the company

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A traveller cheats two Italians out of a clothing firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb here, meaning wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Didicoi is a British term for an itinerant, a member of the travelling community.

clue.text: Lofty dwelling no use for stashing drug? That's life!

indicators.note: stashing means the lofty word hides the drug inside it

parts.note: lofty means high
E is ecstasy

indicators.note: no means the letters of use are taken away

parts.note: a house is a dwelling
taken as written

explanation.surface: A high-rise flat is useless for hiding drugs, a resigned sigh says.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation expresses weary resignation, a sigh meaning such is life.

clue.text: After spillages, glumly await new soup

indicators.note: spillages suggest the letters have been spilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner glumly waits for fresh soup after it was spilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulligatawny is a spicy curry soup from Anglo-Indian cooking.
